forms.form:
te zullen neerkomen
neer te zullen komen

examples.text: De projectielen kwamen neer in een buitenwijk van Kabul.
Paul Krzen liet de bijl weer neerkomen, telkens opnieuw, tot het stuk eiken in tweeën brak.
Een besparing van 20 procent op die kosten zou neerkomen op 46 miljoen.

glosses: To reach by moving down or reducing.

examples.text: Wait for the temperature to come down to a reasonable level before touching the lid.
Come down to my place someday and have lunch.

glosses: To entirely depend upon a single factor; basically, ultimately or in essence.

examples.text: The decision comes down to whether you really want to pay that much for a little extra convenience.
The game is going to come down to the last five seconds.

glosses: To reduce in volume by boiling.

examples.text: He boiled the soup down so it wouldn't be so weak.

glosses: To become reduced (to the most central elements or ingredients: to the essence, core, or implication for action).

examples.text: So what this boils down to is that you still owe me that fifty bucks.
For England, everything now boils down to what happens against Poland on Tuesday.

glosses: To reduce (to the most central elements or ingredients: to the essence, core, or implication for action).

examples.text: My dissertation is 342 pages long, and I'm required to boil it down to a one-page abstract?!
